biography.plain_text: Todd A. Reincke is an American boatyard owner and marine-fabrication specialist who founded Reincke Marine Fabrication on Humboldt Bay. After running yards in Tennessee and Stockton, California, he developed the Fields Landing operation into a full-service facility for commercial vessels. Its work spans haul-outs, metalwork, machinery installation, structural refits and engine work.

long_biography.plain_text:
Reincke Marine Fabrication grew from a do-it-yourself yard at Fields Landing into a full-service repair facility under Todd A. Reincke. Its 150-ton travel lift and enclosed workshop enable his team to haul, extend, repower and refit fishing, recreational and commercial vessels.

Reincke reached Humboldt Bay after fourteen years running a Tennessee boatyard and twelve years at a Stockton yard. His work favours practical conversions, from adding deck space to fishing boats to replacing timber masts with aluminium rigs, alongside machinery installation and high-gloss finishes. The same hands-on approach now anchors a locally based marine business serving vessels across California's North Coast.

uncertainties.detail: The identity is strongly resolved by official permits that place Tod Reincke, Reincke Marine Fabrication and the exact motor vessel BETH together at Humboldt Bay, reinforced by a first-person vessel account and the upstream LinkedIn slug. Current public business and federal records generally use Tod, while the upstream record says Todd A. and the Harbor District's 2020 lease says Todd. No reliable source located expands or independently confirms the middle initial A. The upstream name is preserved because both first-name forms appear in official or authoritative records and the evidence does not justify clearing the middle initial.

The upstream Beth is 32 metres, corresponding closely to the 105-foot BETH in the public record. Harbor District permits directly link Tod Reincke and his business to the named vessel, and a ReinckeMarine forum account says he bought and renamed it. YachtForums is treated only as supporting first-person identity evidence; yacht facts are excluded from biography, industry and wealth classifications.

Reincke's founder-operated marine business and multi-decade boatyard career are well supported, but sources do not establish personal business value, earnings, equity beyond the sole-proprietor structure, starting capital, other holdings or the yard's material contribution to his wealth. Wealth creation and wealth origin therefore remain Unknown rather than treating professional success or yacht ownership as proof of a personal wealth mechanism. No inherited enterprise, pre-existing family asset, succession event, spouse transfer or other family-transfer mechanism was found.

Shipping & Maritime is supported as the current principal business sector by Reincke's continuing control of a substantial full-service marine-repair yard and sole proprietorship. Wealth relationship remains Unknown because the same evidence does not establish that the yard is his principal wealth-producing asset. Founder is used only for the documented business role, known-for title and current Ship repair tag.

National Fisherman reports that Reincke started RMF at Fields Landing roughly four years before its article, after twenty-six years running earlier yards. HigherGov reproduces a federal-registration founding date of 1990 for Tod Reincke's sole proprietorship, which may reflect an earlier business history rather than the current Fields Landing entity. The biographies avoid a specific founding year.

Male gender is supported by consistent direct-reference pronouns in National Fisherman. No sufficiently reliable source established Reincke's title, birthplace, birth date, secondary nationality or secondary residence, so those blanks remain unproposed.

The upstream record marks Reincke Alive. Current industry listings and federal-registration data through 2026 show the exact Tod Reincke business identity, and no credible death report was found. The existing mortality status is preserved without a proposal.

The upstream record already contains a LinkedIn URL with the public Tod spelling, so it is not re-proposed. Yanmar and Seaboard Marine independently verify the company domain, which is proposed only as a Company Website. No identity-secure personal Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website was found.
The mandatory exact-profile and exact-name Forbes checks were performed first for Todd A. Reincke and Tod Reincke, with business and vessel variants. No dedicated Forbes personal profile was found.

Ship repair is the single minimum useful active tag because Reincke has a defining decades-long operating mandate in boatyards and currently owns the full-service RMF yard.
